question.problem:
In an airport, $44%$ of the flights arrive early. Using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution, approximate the probability that if $120$ flights are picked at random, then more than $49$ but less than $70$ will arrive early. Give your answer to three decimal places. *Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.00\,$$\,0.01\,$$\,0.02\,$
$\,-0.7\,$ $\,0.2420\,$ $\,0.2389\,$ $\,0.2358\,$
$\,-0.6\,$ $\,0.2743\,$ $\,0.2709\,$ $\,0.2676\,$
$\,-0.5\,$ $\,0.3085\,$ $\,0.3050\,$ $\,0.3015\,$
$z$$\,0.07\,$$\,0.08\,$$\,0.09\,$
$\,2.9\,$ $\,0.9985\,$ $\,0.9986\,$ $\,0.9986\,$
$\,3.0\,$ $\,0.9989\,$ $\,0.9990\,$ $\,0.9990\,$
$\,3.1\,$ $\,0.9992\,$ $\,0.9993\,$ $\,0.9993\,$
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=120$ and $p=0.44.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =120\cdot 0.44 \\  & =52.8 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =120\cdot (1-0.44) \\  & =67.2 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(120)(0.44)=52.8
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(120)(0.44)(1-0.44)=29.568.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(52.8,29.568).$

Now, we can estimate the desired probability $P(49<X<70).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(49<X<70)=P(50\le X\le 69)≈P(49.5\le Y\le 69.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(49.5\le Y\le 69.5) & =P(\frac{49.5-52.8}{\sqrt{29.568}}\le Z\le \frac{69.5-52.8}{\sqrt{29.568}}) \\  & ≈P(-0.61\le Z\le 3.07) \\  & =P(Z\le 3.07)-P(Z<-0.61) \\  & =P(Z\le 3.07)-P(Z\le -0.61) \\  & =Φ(3.07)-Φ(-0.61) \\  & =0.9989-0.2709 \\  & =0.7280\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(49<X<70)≈0.728.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.7270.$
